newsitem.title: GERMANY: Commerzbank asks clients to judge it.
newsitem.headline: Commerzbank asks clients to judge it.

text.p: Commerzbank AG said on Thursday it would ask all its customers to comment on its service, the latest move in a cultural revolution among German banks seeking to woo clients and become more efficient.
More than one million Commerzbank customers in Germany will be sent questionnaires in what will become an annual survey of customer satisfaction, the bank said in a statement.
Customers will be asked to assess the friendliness and initiative of bank staff, the quality of advice as well as the breadth and availability of services.

Headlined "Your opinion is important to us," Commerzbank's survey is in keeping with sweeping changes among Germany's banks which have realised they must get closer to their clients to boost profitability in their cost-laden branch networks.

Clients long used to inconvenient branch hours and a "take it or leave it" attitude from staff at German banks are being lured by new lower-cost direct banks which offer services like current accounts or share dealing by telephone, pc or fax.
Commerzbank as well its larger rivals Deutsche Bank AG and Dresdner Bank AG are now opening branches longer and Deutsche last week opened its first "bankingshop" -- a bank branch in a supermarket.
Commerzbank said it had surveyed customers at selected branches since 1993 and mostly received good marks but had taken steps to improve itself when it was criticised.
The new annual surveys will be used to help assess staff and determine performance related pay, Commerzbank said.
"That creates incentives for staff to see themselves even more as service providers for the customers," Commerzbank said.
